To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

there are few approaches that perform a model driven requirements engineering for software product lines, and the approaches that do not use a model driven approach for requirements engineering, use a model driven development for other phases of the SPL development.
the current state of the art of MDE approaches for RE for SPL is still immature.

the current approaches for requirements engineering for SPLs are mainly focused on the Domain engineering phase and use model transformations to obtain requirements artifacts, and there is a lack on the tool support for the requirements specification and management.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the current state-of-the-art of MDE-based approaches for RE in SPL.
the identification of current practices and research challenges to improve the requirements engineering for software product lines in a model driven context.
identifying the state of the art in the application of MDE in the RE activity of SPL, and the main research gaps to be explored in future research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is still a lot of work to do in the field.
there is a lack in the state of the art of a well established and consolidated approach to perform RE in SPL using MDE, with a clear definition of the artifacts and the processes involved.
most of the proposals are focused on the domain engineering phase of the development, and they do not consider the application engineering phase in the RE activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a need to improve and validate the current proposals for model-driven requirements engineering for SPL, in order to make them applicable in industrial contexts.
the approaches are not well supported in the Application Engineering phase, and the lack of empirical evidence is a major concern.
the approaches are still in an early stage and there are still many open issues to be addressed in the RE activity in the context of SPL development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a lack in the state-of-the-art of approaches to manage requirements for SPL in a model driven way.
the RE community should focus on the development of tools and techniques that support the RE activity for model driven product line developments.
the RE activity for MDE-based SPL development is not sufficiently covered by current approaches.
